Databricks signed a term sheet at $188 billion on July 17, 40% above its last completed mark.

Coatue leads, with new and existing investors behind it, and press reports put the size near $3 billion.[1][3] The close is expected later this summer; until funds settle, the $134 billion February mark anchors the base case.
The same $6.9 billion run-rate now carries two prices: 19.4x at the completed mark, 27.2x at the announced one.
No operating number moved with the announcement, so the September print decides which multiple the buyer actually paid.[7]
Revenue is accelerating through $7 billion: four straight prints, +50% to +80% YoY.
The counterweight is gross margin at 74%, guided lower, four points above the 70% floor that forces a quality re-score no matter what the round does.[7]
At either mark, Databricks is the cheapest quality-adjusted asset in the cohort: $15.2 billion per point of business quality completed, about $21.3 billion announced (est.).
The nearest peer pays about $118 billion per point. We assess a close by October 31 as very likely (80-95%). Confidence: moderate; the size and terms are press-sourced.[3]
